views.note: xml_loc=187. wizard/homework_location_wizard.xml declares the wizard form (date / weekly toggle / 'Repeat every <weekday>' / work_location_id + a 'Set Location' button calling set_employee_location) and a window action set_location_wizard_action (target='new', binding_model_id=homework.location.wizard). behavioral_notes.element: homework.location.wizard.set_employee_location — the create/update/delete-exception engine (the module's core write path)
behavioral_notes.observation: This TransientModel method is where every calendar edit lands; it is the substance of the add-on and is invisible to metadata. ensure_one(); returns early if no date. It resolves the target employee from self.employee_id or context default_employee_id (fallback env.user.employee_id), then searches the existing hr.employee.location for (date, employee). weekday = self.date.weekday(); default_location_for_current_date = DAYS[weekday]. Branch A (self.weekly=True): it deletes any dated exception on that date, then writes the weekday default through the USER record — employee_id.sudo().user_id.write({DAYS[weekday]: work_location_id}) — i.e. 'weekly/recurring' means setting the day-of-week default (related-synced to hr.employee), NOT creating a calendar.event. Branch B (one-off): if the chosen work_location_id equals the employee's existing weekday default it UNLINKS the exception (no redundant exception row); elif an exception already exists it WRITEs it; else it CREATEs a new hr.employee.location row for that date. So the wizard is the single place that reconciles the two-layer model and prunes exceptions that match the default. None of this branching/pruning is expressible in metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: hr.employee._get_worklocation(start_date, end_date) — the calendar feed assembling weekly defaults + exceptions
behavioral_notes.observation: The OWL calendar's data source. For each employee it seeds a dict with user_id, employee_id, partner_id (user_partner_id or work_contact_id), employee_name, then for every day in DAYS emits {location_type, location_name, work_location_id} from that weekday's default m2o (employee[day]). It then search_reads hr.employee.location for that employee set within [start_date, end_date] and folds each dated row into an 'exceptions'[date] sub-dict keyed by DEFAULT_SERVER_DATE_FORMAT date string, carrying hr_employee_location_id so the front end can tell a real exception row (editable/deletable) from a synthesised weekly-default 'ghost'. res.partner.get_worklocation is the public entry the JS RPC-calls: it search()es hr.employee by ('work_contact_id','in',partner_ids) scoped to env.company and delegates here. This server-built merge of recurring + exceptional locations into a calendar payload is pure Python.

behavioral_notes.element: calendar integration is a VIEW overlay, not calendar.event rows (AttendeeCalendarModel / Controller JS patches)
behavioral_notes.observation: Despite depends=['calendar'], this module creates NO calendar.event records (grep confirms calendar.event appears only in a test mock). Instead static/src/calendar/common/* PATCHES the calendar app: AttendeeCalendarModel.prototype.updateData/loadWorkLocations calls res.partner.get_worklocation and synthesises virtual day-cells — createHomeworkingRecordAt builds records with resModel:'hr.employee.location', homeworking:true, and a ghostRecord flag (id 'default-location-<emp>-<ms>' when there is no hr_employee_location_id, i.e. the cell is just the weekly default). AttendeeCalendarController.prototype.editRecord routes a click on a homeworking cell to action hr_homeworking_calendar.set_location_wizard_action (passing default_date/default_work_location_id); deleteRecord, for a ghostRecord, writes res.users.<weekday>_location_id = False (clearing the weekly default), otherwise orm.unlink('hr.employee.location', id) (removing just that exception). So the 'calendar' is the standard attendee calendar repainted with work-location ghosts, and edits flow back through the wizard / direct ORM — a behavior only the JS reveals.

behavioral_notes.element: homework.location.wizard._compute_day_week_string + wizard form binding (UX semantics of the 'weekly' toggle)
behavioral_notes.observation: _compute_day_week_string (@api.depends('date')) renders the date's weekday name via tools.format_date(..., 'EEEE') or '' when no date, which the wizard form (wizard/homework_location_wizard.xml) interpolates into the 'Repeat every <day_week_string>' label next to the weekly checkbox — so ticking 'weekly' visibly promises 'every <Monday>' before set_employee_location runs Branch A. The action set_location_wizard_action is target='new' and bound (binding_model_id) so it opens as a dialog; the JS passes default_date and default_work_location_id into its context, which the wizard fields default from. This date->weekday-label coupling and the context-driven defaulting are behavioral glue not shown by field metadata.

behavioral_notes.element: frontend (static) — patched attendee calendar (renderers, year view, popover)
behavioral_notes.observation: 5 JS files, 0 OWL components, 0 registry adds, 6 prototype patches (gap #3). Beyond the model/controller above, calendar_common_renderer.js / calendar_year_renderer.js patch AttendeeCalendarCommonRenderer / AttendeeCalendarYearRenderer to draw the work-location ghost cells, and popover/calendar_common_popover.js patches AttendeeCalendarCommonPopover to show location details + the edit/delete affordances. The 'services' date/weekday/weekly reported by extract are template/prop hooks, not Odoo registry services. Bundles: web.assets_backend, web.assets_unit_tests. The whole work-location calendar UX lives in these patches over the calendar module and is unreachable from Python metadata (gap #3).

Edit the schedule from the calendar via a single dialog (homework.location.wizard)
Set a recurring weekday default ('weekly') or a one-day exception from the same dialog
Prune redundant exceptions automatically (an exception equal to the weekday default is removed)
Delete a day's location (clear the weekly default or remove just the exception)

Weekly default work location (7 day-of-week fields, owned by hr_homeworking)
Attendee calendar work-location cell (virtual, resModel hr.employee.location, ghost vs real)
organization: (no module-owned res.groups; base.group_user runs the wizard for self, hr.group_hr_user for anyone)

'weekly' sets the recurring weekday default and deletes any conflicting same-date exception; one-off creates/updates an exception
An exception equal to that weekday's default is not stored (set_employee_location unlinks it) — exceptions are only deviations
Deleting a ghost (default) cell clears the weekly default field; deleting a real cell unlinks only that hr.employee.location row

classification.rationale: hr_homeworking_calendar is a thin UX/integration layer on top of hr_homeworking, so it inherits the same classification. It owns no persistent business object — its only declared model is a TransientModel (homework.location.wizard, 8 fields) plus two _inherit-only models adding the calendar-feed methods; 0 routes, 1 ACL + 2 ir.rule, ~336 py LOC, auto_install=true, application=false, category Human Resources/Remote Work. By Stabell & Fjeldstad it is a SUPPORT activity (workforce administration; it produces no product, solves no client problem, brokers no network) and a Porter HR/infrastructure support activity. APQC 7.0 Develop and Manage Human Capital fits for the same reason as its parent: it captures and presents where employees work (the 7.x employee-information / workforce-management nuance), here adding a calendar view and an edit dialog over that schedule. Notably the 'calendar' dependency is purely the attendee-calendar UI being patched (no calendar.event is created), so this is not a scheduling/event-management capability in its own right. 8.0 Manage IT was rejected (no IT-service plumbing, no routes, no external calls); it is the presentation/editing tier of an HR people-data feature, hence 7.0.

standard_capabilities: Attendee-calendar rendering of the per-employee remote-work schedule (multi-employee, year + common views)
homework.location.wizard dialog to set a weekly default or a dated exception from the calendar
Automatic pruning of exceptions that match the weekday default
Delete affordances: clear the weekly default (ghost cell) or remove a single exception
Server-side merge of weekly defaults + exceptions into one calendar feed (get_worklocation)
typical_fits: Teams that want to see and edit hybrid/remote days on the same calendar they use for meetings
Letting employees self-schedule remote days by clicking the calendar (self-only via ir.rule)
HR adjusting many employees' office/home days visually
common_gaps: No calendar.event is created, so the schedule does NOT appear in external/synced calendars (Google/Outlook) or block meeting availability
Inherits hr_homeworking's one-location-per-day limit (the wizard writes a single hr.employee.location per date)
Editing is dialog-based per day; there is no drag-to-recur or range edit
All UX lives in JS patches over the calendar module, so a future calendar-app refactor can break it (tight coupling, gap #3)
No approval/notification when a remote day is set
